key_insight: Simulated liquid-metal electrode swirl follows a Ruelle–Takens–Newhouse route to chaos, with an intermediate strange non-chaotic attractor regime and transitions organized by the Lorentz-to-viscous force ratio Q_m.
engineering_relevance: Mapping magnetic-field-driven flow transitions can help engineers anticipate unsteady mixing in liquid metal battery electrodes.
method: Run three-dimensional simulations of electromagnetically driven swirl in cylindrical electrodes.
Vary magnetic field (0.1–20 G), current (11.11–100 A), radius (3–9 cm), and height (3 or 4.5 cm).
Diagnose transitions using phase portraits, FFT spectra, the 0–1 chaos test, autocorrelation, and correlation dimension.
evidence_signal: Across simulated geometries and forcing conditions, oscillatory onset occurs at nearly invariant Q_m for fixed aspect ratio except when height changes, while Reynolds number follows Re ∼ Q_m^(2/3).
watch_item: Transition thresholds depend on geometry and forcing; the abstract reports simulation evidence rather than experimental validation.
paper_title: Transition to turbulence in swirl created by a vertical magnetic field in liquid metal electrodes
